metadata.case_name: RUKHSAR BEGUM v. NATIVE ENGLISH CENTER LIMITED trading as THE GREEN LOUNGE

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: teacher (intend to study for a teaching-related diploma at Hong Kong Open University)

injuries.description: fracture of the base of the distal phalanx of the right ring finger (healed with mild mal-union)
source: for the finger injury, contrary to the diagnosis made by the government doctors, Dr Li found, after reviewing the X–ray films of the right ring finger, that there was in fact a fracture of the base of the distal phalanx of the finger even though the fracture had already healed quite well with mild mal-union at the time of his review of the films. The mal-union, in Dr Lis opinion, may potentially cause residual symptoms.

injuries.description: meniscal tear of the right knee (classified as "grade 2")
source: Dr Li classified the meniscal tear of the right knee as grade 2[12].
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the knee or lower leg

source: She was found by the physiotherapist to have suffered from right traumatic patellar tendinitis [4]
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of muscle, fascia or tendon of anterior muscle group at lower leg level

manifestations.description: tender and swollen right ring finger and knee
reduced range of movement of right knee
mild stiffness of right ring finger
discomfort from continuous bending or standing for 4 hours or more

treatments_received.treatment: treated and discharged with a knee brace and walking stick
source: She was treated and discharged with a knee brace and walking stick[3] on the same day.

treatments_received.treatment: follow-up consultations at Orthopaedics & Traumatology Department, Queen Mary Hospital on 2 December 2013, 24 February 2014, 3 March 2014 and 23 June 2014
source: Upon referral, Ms Begum attended four follow-up sessions with the Orthopaedics & Traumatology Department (O & T) of Queen Mary Hospital on 2 December 2013, 24 February, 3 March and 23 June 2014, and two physiotherapy treatments for her knee injury on 16 and 23 December 2013.

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy (two treatments on 16 December 2013 and 23 December 2013)
source: Upon referral, Ms Begum attended four follow-up sessions with the Orthopaedics & Traumatology Department (O & T) of Queen Mary Hospital on 2 December 2013, 24 February, 3 March and 23 June 2014, and two physiotherapy treatments for her knee injury on 16 and 23 December 2013.

treatments_received.treatment: MRI scan of the right knee (private) on 15 January 2014
source: On 15 January 2014, Ms Begum had an MRI scan of the right knee done privately.

treatments_future.treatment: conservative treatment to strengthen the right ring finger using "Power Putty" (total cost $450)
source: Dr Li recommended Ms Begum to undergo conservative treatment to strengthen the finger function by doing exercises at home with the use of a gadget called Power Putty (at the total cost of $450 for the entire set).

treatments_future.treatment: non-surgical conservative treatment for right knee to recover strength and endurance
source: Instead of suggesting that Ms Begum undergo an arthroscopy for assessing the extent of tear and repair as he had previously stated in Lis 1st, Dr Li, after having seen the MRI films, opined in Lis 2nd [13] that Ms Begum should recover the normal strength and endurance of the knee by non-surgical conservative treatment.
In Lis 1st, 12 sessions are being recommended.

losses.description: Mild mal-union of the base of the distal phalanx of the right ring finger may potentially cause residual symptoms
Grade 2 meniscal tear of the right knee causing right knee pain, decreased range of motion and limping gait
Unable to resume pre-accident waitressing job due to residual pain in the right knee
Reduced ability to stand or continuously bend for 4 hours or more and initial limitation to walk unaided for only about 15 minutes with a limping gait
